predecessors.name: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
predecessors.text: the northern Netherlands of the Sovereign Principality (Cliopatria 1814 shape, 35,750 km2)

ledger.x: 1815: William Frederick is proclaimed King William I of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands in Brussels.
ledger.cpn: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands

ledger.x: 1815: the southern Netherlands are joined to the kingdom.
1815: William I gains the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg in personal union.
1830: Dutch troops keep the Antwerp citadel inside the new Belgium.
1830: Belgium claims the whole Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
1830: the Dutch army holds Maastricht and the rest of Limburg is disputed.
1830: Belgium secedes.
1831: the Dutch army invades Belgium (Ten Days' Campaign).
1831: the offensive fails after French intervention.
1832: the Antwerp citadel falls.
1839: the Grand Duchy is partitioned.
1839: the western Grand Duchy passes to Belgium.
1839: the Treaty of London ends the Luxembourg dispute.
1839: Limburg is split and the Dutch part confirmed.
1839: the Limburg dispute ends.
1839: the rump Grand Duchy remains in personal union with the Dutch king.
1890: the personal union with Luxembourg ends.
1940: Germany invades and occupies the Netherlands.
1945: the Netherlands are freed.
1949: the Netherlands annex German border land.
1963: the annexed land is returned.
2010: the Caribbean Netherlands join the country proper.

wars.name: Belgian Revolution
wars.outcome: Belgium became independent (declared 4 October 1830) and the Treaty of London of 19 April 1839 recognised it; the Netherlands kept Maastricht and eastern Limburg and the Grand Duchy was partitioned.

wars.name: Ten Days' Campaign
wars.outcome: The Dutch offensive failed after French intervention of 9 August 1831; the page names no ground kept.

wars.name: Battle of the Netherlands
wars.outcome: German victory; the Dutch forces surrendered on 15 May 1940 after the bombing of Rotterdam and the country was occupied until 1945.

wars.name: Liberation of the Netherlands
wars.outcome: Allied forces entered at Mesch on 12 September 1944, Maastricht was the first city liberated (13-14 September) and the German surrender at Wageningen on 5 May 1945 freed the whole country.

certainty.note: The Congress of Vienna and the 1815 constitution fix the kingdom; the Luxembourg frontier is a German Confederation border.

Belgian frontier de facto and disputed until the Treaty of London of 19 April 1839; the detailed line was fixed by the Treaty of Maastricht (1843), so 1839-1842 is a settled but not yet surveyed frontier.
Treaty frontiers with Belgium and Germany; the 1949-1963 German border annexation and the 1940-1945 occupation are the exceptions.
